submitter: bugfix_165 session (site A: page_components completeness floor)
rationale: bugs_open/165 site A, filed at this council's own bug_historian seat's direction in round 2 of corr 14239fa4-552f-4821-abaf-ea15ccee4ea5. bugs_closed/135 built a tested completeness floor for code_symbols and deliberately left three mechanistically identical reconciliation deletes unguarded. The seat's objection was that stopping there IS the platform's most repeated pattern ('one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix; the sibling stays heuristic', 016b §9, index title 021_HANDOFF_2026-07-18_durable_write_guard_covers_one_path_only). This converts the highest-stakes of the three: SavePageSectionsAction deletes every agent-writable page_components row for a page and re-inserts the section set it was handed, with NOTHING checking that the run saw the whole page. The section set comes from an LLM writer, or from regex-parsing assembled HTML on the fallback path; both return a short-but-nonzero result with no error, and the outcome is not a broken row but ABSENCE, which reads as 'there was never anything there'. This is the table that has actually lost customer-facing content: 016b §9 cases 1 and 2 (an A* pathfinding game destroyed by exactly this DELETE+INSERT, recurring independently on a second site), plus case files 001, 037, 038 and bugs_closed/058. The existing guards do not cover it and cannot: pageComponentAgentWritableSQL is an AUTHORITY check (may I delete this row?) which a writer returning two sections instead of twelve passes perfectly; the text and interactivity regression guards read build_status='deployed' only, and 142 of the 426 pages that have components have no deployed row at all, so on a third of the corpus they are blind; and the text guard compares CHARACTERS, so two verbose sections replacing twelve concise ones clear its quarter-of-existing bar while dropping ten. The cohorts here were chosen AFTER reading the live distribution, not from the shape of the SQL — 165 says in terms that guessing them is how a guard that fires on legitimate edits gets built and then deleted by the first person it blocks. Two candidate cohort shapes were measured and REJECTED on the data, and the plan-side denominator was measured WRONG first and corrected; both are recorded below because they are the load-bearing part of the design.

plan.summary: Add a measured completeness floor to save_page_sections' reconciliation delete, reusing bugs_closed/135's rule (evaluatePruneFloor, CTXA-025) unchanged. Two cohorts, both chosen from the live distribution: rows (what this save will insert vs the rows the DELETE would remove) and plan (vs pages.sections, less suppressed, less locked). Refuses the whole save rather than skipping the delete, because here the delete and the insert are one operation. Fails closed on an unmeasurable floor, resolvable by step config, durable refusal in site_work_items.

edits.rationale: The measurement and the wiring, in its own file beside the sibling guards (save_sections_claims_guard.go, save_sections_link_repair.go). It ADDS A CONSUMER to 135's rule and changes nothing about the rule itself — evaluatePruneFloor, pruneCohort, pruneFloorFromConfig and defaultPruneFloorRatio are used exactly as shipped, so no guarantee of the shared mechanism moves. TWO COHORTS, both measured (see grounded_in): 'sections' is the row unit, what this save will insert against the rows the DELETE would remove; 'planned sections' is the PLAN unit, and it is what breaks the RATCHET — once a truncating writer has cut a page from twelve rows to two, the row cohort reads 2/2 = 100% for ever and the damage becomes the new baseline, while the plan still reads 2 of 12. pages.sections is written by seven OTHER actions and never by this one, so it is a genuinely independent statement of intent rather than an echo of what this action last wrote.

The stored count is built from pageComponentAgentWritableSQL — the SAME helper the DELETE's own predicate is built from, not a hand-rolled equivalent. Any other spelling is a second predicate free to drift from the one being guarded, and a guard measuring a different population from the one at risk is worse than none: it reports a confident ratio for rows nobody was going to delete. This is 135's stated discipline (`IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2`, the exact complement of the DELETE's `IS DISTINCT FROM $2`) applied to a different predicate.
edits.sketch:
(SELECT count(*) FROM page_components pc
   WHERE pc.page_id = p.id AND `+pageComponentAgentWritableSQL("pc.")+`)

edits.rationale: The floor is placed LAST of the refusal guards and immediately before the first write. Last, because it is the only guard needing the FINAL section set: the interactive-tool preservation (Layer 2) re-appends sections a rebuild dropped, and a floor measured before that would refuse a save the preservation had already repaired. Before the history snapshot, so a refused save writes nothing whatever — not even a history row recording content it never went on to replace. loadActiveLockedRows moves up ~35 lines (a read-only query; nothing between changes lock state) because the floor's numerator needs to know how many incoming sections a lock will swallow.

Extracts the bugs_open/039 skip predicate (`componentIDPtr == nil && isEmptyGenericStub(html)`) so the insert loop and the floor decide by the SAME rule. They MUST agree: the floor counts what this save will write, and a section the loop is about to discard is not written. Two copies of this condition sixty lines apart is precisely the drift class this council reviews for, and the failure would be silent and one-directional — a floor counting discarded stubs as confirmed content is permissive in the one direction it must not be wrong in.

The floor's numbers are reported on a PASSING save too, not only on refusal. `sections_saved: 2` without its denominator is the alarm presented as output — candidate (3) of 135, restated for this table — and it is the reason orchestration_states cannot today answer 'was that rebuild thin?' after the fact.
edits.sketch: for k, v := range floorDetail { result[k] = v }

edits.rationale: The DURABLE surface. site_work_items rather than 135's doc_notes, because this writer IS site-scoped and the NOT NULL columns are in hand — 135 fell back to doc_notes only because a repo-wide indexer has no site, and 165 notes the difference explicitly. Routing mirrors the lock-blocked family: status 'needs_human_review' with NO handler_agent, because whether a page genuinely shrank by half is a human judgement no automated handler can make. Goes through insertWorkItem so it inherits the idx_swi_dedup-matched ON CONFLICT (no 42P10 drift) and the two-strike rule; item_key is per page, so a page failing every rebuild collapses to one open item. Best-effort: a failure here is logged and swallowed, since the refusal is already carried by the returned error.
edits.sketch:
itemType: "save_refused_incomplete", severity: "high", status: "needs_human_review",
itemKey: fmt.Sprintf("save_refused_incomplete:%s", pageName)

edits.rationale: Every refusal test was checked by BREAKING the thing it guards and watching it fail — four mutations, each applied to a fresh baseline in an isolated `git archive HEAD` tree, each failing exactly the test that guards it and only that test. The package landmine is why: a test asserting a query is NOT issued passes vacuously against insertWorkItem, which swallows the mock's error. So the refusal tests pin the INSERT's own status argument rather than its existence. The two tests to keep if any are ever cut are TestPageSectionFloorPassesAHealthyRebuildOfALockedPage (the locked-denominator correction) and TestPageSectionFloorCatchesTheRatchetTheRowCohortMisses (why there are two cohorts at all).

grounded_in: The delete as it stands, guarded by nothing: `DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1 AND `+pageComponentAgentWritableSQL("") — save_page_sections_action.go:532, preceded only by authority and character-count guards.

REJECTED COHORT SHAPE 1, per-slot_name (which bugs_open/165 itself suggested as 'plausibly one cohort per slot_name'). Measured: 998 of 1,009 (page_id, slot_name) groups hold exactly ONE row (7 hold two, 4 hold three). Every per-slot cohort would therefore be 1 stored, so dropping a single section legitimately scores that cohort 0% and refuses the save. page_component_history shows 89 such legitimate shrinkages in 4.5 months, every one of which this shape would have blocked. This is the measurement that killed the shape the bug file proposed.
REJECTED COHORT SHAPE 2, per-component_id: 365 of 409 pages have as many distinct component_ids as rows, so it is the row count in a costume and carries no independent signal.

KEPT COHORT 1 false-positive rate, the row unit. Across 2,620 consecutive overwrite pairs in page_component_history (source='save_page_sections_overwrite', 2026-03-16 to 2026-07-31), 89 shrank at all, and at a 0.5 floor exactly 4 fall below it — 0.15% of real rebuilds. At 0.34 it is 1; at 0.25, none. [PROXY: 'after' is the next event's snapshot, which excludes rows with empty rendered_html and includes locked rows, so it approximates rather than reproduces the written count.]

KEPT COHORT 2 is not an echo: pages.sections is written by load_page_sections_from_spec_action.go:153,214,364, apply_gap_plan_action.go:429,647, apply_adoption_plan_action.go:534, create_blog_posts_action.go:222, deploy_tool_action.go:379, create_report_page_action.go:166 and adopt_verbatim.go:475 — and by NO path in save_page_sections. A grep of every `UPDATE pages`/`INSERT INTO pages` touching the column confirms it.

THE DENOMINATOR CORRECTION, and the reason to distrust the first version of this plan. My first plan denominator was the raw planned count. Measured against production it tripped on 3 pages; opening the rows rather than trusting the count showed idea.uk/index.html plans 6 sections and HOLDS 4 LOCKS, so a perfect rebuild writes 2 and would have scored 2/6 = 33% and been REFUSED — a guard that blocks every rebuild of exactly the pages a human cared enough about to lock. With locked rows excluded the cohort trips on 0 of the 238 reachable pages. (The 2 that still trip are rebuild_policy='owned', which this action refuses ~370 lines earlier at save_page_sections_action.go:150.)

The existing guards' measured blind spot: 142 of the 426 pages that have components have NO row with build_status='deployed', and both the content-regression guard (save_page_sections_action.go:408) and the interactivity guard (:448) scope their existence check to `build_status = 'deployed'`. On a third of the corpus neither can fire at all.

Live page sizes, which is why the cohorts are page-level and small-N: of 409 pages with agent-writable rows, 178 have exactly 1, 51 have 2, 98 have 3, and the maximum is 8. A per-class partition of a 3-row page is not a partition.
suppressed_sections is a real but tiny confound — 4 pages carry any, maximum 2 each — so it is subtracted for correctness rather than because it moves a number today.
The lineage for the stakes: 016b §9 cases 1 and 2, plus bugs_closed/058 (rebuild path did not honour page_component locks), 001, 037, 038.
The rule being reused, unchanged: platform/orchestration/actions/prune_floor.go, register CTXA-025, closed case bugs_closed/135 (live on chassis v1.0.1218, both branches induced in production).
plan.risks:
1. THE CONSUMERS, NAMED AND TOLD (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §3). Six live agents gain a new refusal path: page-build-handler, pageflow-builder, page-rebuild, page-rerender, site-work-orchestrator, tool-recreation-handler. Measured by counting the exact key text `"action": "save_page_sections"` in each active, non-snapshot agent_definitions row — NOT by the step-level census, which returns only 3 because pageflow-builder and page-rebuild nest the step inside a loop (the bugs_open/086-087 landmine). What changes about their guarantee: a rebuild that produces less than half of what a page stores, or less than half of what it plans, now FAILS the step instead of silently replacing the page. They are told in the 165 case file and in this lane's README.

2. FALSE REFUSAL on a genuine large shrink. Measured at 4 in 2,620 real rebuilds (0.15%) for the row cohort and 0 of 238 reachable pages for the plan cohort. Consequence is a failed build step and an unchanged live page, not lost content; resolvable per step via prune_floor_ratio (0 disables). The refusal text states that remedy itself, because a refusal a reader cannot act on gets overridden by someone deleting the guard.

3. THE REFUSAL IS HARSHER THAN 135'S, and this is the material difference to judge. 135 refuses the prune and lets the run continue, which is self-healing — a later healthy run prunes what was retained. Here the delete and the insert are ONE operation: refusing the delete but performing the insert would write new sections alongside the old, which is bugs_open/156's duplicate-page_components defect. So the whole save is refused, exactly as the three sibling regression guards in this file already do. A false refusal therefore costs a build step rather than nothing.

4. FAIL-CLOSED ON AN UNMEASURABLE FLOOR means a DB error at this point fails the page build. Accepted: the measurement is the only thing between a half-blind writer and a stripped page, and a transient error here would very likely fail the following DELETE/INSERT anyway. The alternative — proceeding unguarded when the guard cannot see — reintroduces exactly the defect.

5. SCOPE. This adds a CONSUMER of an existing shared rule and changes nothing about the rule, so no guarantee of the shared mechanism moves (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1: additive-and-inert is not architecture-scope; the RFC trigger is a change to what the shared mechanism GUARANTEES). It does change a guarantee for the six consumers of save_page_sections above, which is why they are named rather than merely counted. Sites B (populate_nav_tables, site_nav_items/groups) and C (site_db_actions:1474, link_registry) remain OPEN in bugs_open/165 and are deliberately NOT converted here — B is live territory for the bugfix_149_nav_membership lane, and both need their own cohorts measured, not copied from this one.
